fixes_in_this_run.Codex 4 backups.go create audits only af: POST /api/v1/backups writes a backup_request intent row before calling the supervisor; when that write fails no backup is made. Afterwards it appends the outcome under the same request id: created (backup id) plus the backup row with its SHA-256, or failed with the supervisor's error. An outcome-write failure is logged and the created backup is still reported (202). Test: TestBackupCreateAuditsIntentBeforeTheSupervisor (intent refused: supervisor never called; outcome refused: 202 with the backup; normal and supervisor-refused outcomes), plus test-backup-e2e.sh now asserts the archive holds exactly the intent row and no outcome row.
fixes_in_this_run.Codex 5 supervisor operations.go restore: With writers stopped and before the swap, checkFileExport (internal/supervisor/filestage.go) reads the whole export: manifest first, every object listed once with its size and SHA-256, none missing. A bad set fails with invalid_backup while the existing database is live, and the core is never handed it; a good set is spooled. Only the restarted core can write the bytes (it holds the backends' credentials and reads locations from the restored database), so the write still follows the restart. If it fails, the record is marked failed (files_not_restored), then the safety backup taken just before the swap is restored as its own journaled restore (source rollback:<id>) through the existing stop, swap and restart path, and the record's error becomes files_rolled_back. If the rollback fails, the error stays files_not_restored and the admin is mailed. 690f8ae then writes the bytes on every path that ends a committed swap (finishApplied, finishCleanup, startup recovery of an applied or committed record); the journal records the pending export (files, files_safety) before the swap and clears it only after the write, so a supervisor restarted after the swap rolls back instead of completing without the bytes. 08cb908 holds users out of the restored core until then (see the restore-hold entry), so the rollback loses no user write. Ceiling (PONYTAIL-DEBT.md Platform 18): only a rollback that also fails, or a supervisor that never answers the core. Tests: TestRestoreRefusesADamagedFileExportBeforeTheSwap (bytes differ, object missing, size differs, no manifest: no dump, core not handed, writers restarted), TestRestoreFileWriteFailureRollsBackTheSwap, TestRestoreFileWriteFailureWithAFailedRollbackIsReported, and TestRestoreHandsTheFilesToTheRestartedCore on a real export. Added in 690f8ae: TestRestoreCleanupPendingStillWritesTheFiles, TestRestoreCleanupPendingFileWriteFailureRollsBack, TestRecoveryAfterRestartRollsBackALostFileExport, TestRecoveryCompletesACommittedRestoreWhoseFilesWereWritten.

fixes_in_this_run.Codex review of 49ebc19 (P1) restored co: 08cb908, the third and last pass on finding 5, approved by Patrick 2026-11-14 06:38 UTC. A core with a supervisor starts held: until the supervisor's new GET /v1/restores/hold answers false it serves only /api/v1/health, /healthz and the supervisor-token file import at /internal/v1/file-bytes, answers every other request (API, MCP, module routes, screens) with 503 restore_in_progress, and starts no background worker (module event pump, webhooks, marketplace check, document worker, trust mail). The first answer is awaited before the core listens; then it asks every second, and it stays held while the supervisor does not answer. The supervisor holds while a file export is spooled, while any non-terminal journal record says its files are pending, and while a file rollback runs (Operations.FileHold); an unreadable journal holds. Tests: TestRestoreHoldKeepsUsersOutUntilTheFilesAreBack and TestRestoreHoldOpensAtOnceWhenNothingHolds (core, real Postgres), TestRestoreHoldsUsersOutUntilTheFilesAreWritten, TestRestoreHoldStandsThroughTheFileRollback and TestRestoreHoldSurvivesASupervisorRestart (supervisor). earlier_work_kept_on_this_branch: Previous pass (tested 4697f27, reviewed head f4f9222 found its code sound): P1 internal/core/app.go MigrateSealed unseal window: core migrate no longer hands the append-only tables to togavsu_app for the run. db.ApplySealed (internal/db/ledgers.go) runs the migrations on one superuser session switched to the application role with SET ROLE, so every object a migration creates still belongs to togavsu_app. A migration whose SQL names an append-only table gets only those tables handed to togavsu_app at the start of its own transaction, and ledgerseal.Script seals them again before that transaction commits. Postgres DDL is transactional, so no other session, including the old core serving during an update, ever sees a ledger it could change, and a failed, cancelled or killed migration rolls the handoff back. Migrations that name no ledger run with no handoff and take no lock on the ledgers. With nothing pending, core migrate only re-runs the seal, which also repairs a database an older core migrate left unsealed. db.UnsealLedgers is removed. Regression tests: TestLedgersSealedForApplicationRole fails a ledger migration (1/0 after an ALTER), then kills the migrating backend with pg_terminate_backend mid-migration, checks with db.VerifySealed on the application role's connection that the ledgers are sealed while it runs and after it dies, and that neither column exists; an expand migration still applies through db.ApplySealed and the admin pool session returns as the superuser. TestWrapLedgerMigration checks where the handoff and seal go in the Up section, that only named tables are handed over, and that unrelated migrations are unchanged. The remaining lock window is recorded as a second ceiling on PONYTAIL-DEBT.md Contracts item 4.
